newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon growth down in Q1 - Banque Audi.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon growth down in Q1 - Banque Audi.

text.p: Banque Audi said in its latest economic report Lebanon's economic growth fell in the first quarter below last year's four percent annual growth rate.
"Growth in the first quarter of 1997 slowed down significantly. In terms of annual rates, it fell from the four percent reported in 1996," the report said.
"Internal sources of growth appeared to have run dry. Consumption was sluggish and investment fell."

In a break with its usual practice, Banque Audi did not give a figure for first quarter growth. However, it referred to "relative stagnation" in comparison with the first quarter of 1996 when it reported growth at three percent.

An annualised growth of less than three percent would be the lowest growth Lebanon has experienced since billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri took over in October 1992 with a mandate to rebuild the country after the 1975-90 civil war.
It compares with a growth target of 10 percent a year set in Hariri's multi-billion dollars reconstruction programme.

Banque Audi said sluggish consumption and disappointing demand in the first quarter resulted from "depression in the political and business environments" and the cumulative effects of the government's adjustment policies.
Industry continued to sell off stocks and investment fell, it said.

"Compared to the first quarter of 1996, both public and private investment decreased, according to our estimates, by almost 14 percent in nominal value, thus negatively affecting growth and confirming the slowing down of activity."
Other indicators included a continual decline in the growth of bank loans to the private sector and deterioration of the state's debt ratios.

The 59.67 percent first quarter budget deficit of income against expenditure, compared with the planned 36 percent, was due both to insufficient revenue caused by economic stagnation and to the weak, 13 percent ratio of public receipts to GDP, the report said.
